subject: On-prem addendum: license scope, evidence transfer & operator access
messages:
From: Emma Clark <emma.clark@nextherahealth.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: patrick.owens@nextherahealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Private deploy addendum — license boundary and evidence request

Aisha,

Thanks for taking this. We’re working through legal for our planned on-prem deployment of Redwood inside our regulated environment. A few high-level asks from NexThera Legal to get in scope before we proceed to procurement: 

- Clear licensed scope: will Redwood grant a perpetual runtime license to the deployed image in our on-prem environment, or is this a time-limited runtime? We need explicit territory and transfer terms for our internal auditors.
- Operator access: what level of access will Redwood staff retain for troubleshooting? We need an auditable, time-limited process.
- Evidence / escrow-like capability: our compliance team prefers an option to receive an attested read-only snapshot and a signed statement of access controls (quarterly or on-demand for incident response).
- Audit windows: preferred frequency and how logs/evidence will be transferred.
- KMS/HSM custody: what are the supported models for key custody if we require split-control?

I’ve attached a short list of questions (NexThera_Questions_v1.pdf) and a preliminary redline from our side will follow. Can we get a first-pass position from Redwood legal and engineering by EOD Thursday?

Best,
Emma Clark
Senior Counsel — Regulatory & Privacy
NexThera Health
attachments: NexThera_Questions_v1.pdf
From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Clark <emma.clark@nextherahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:27:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deploy addendum — license boundary and evidence request

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (contracts) and Laura (legal) to own the redlines — I’ll own the deployment and runbook pieces from an engineering/ops perspective. High-level Redwood positions to start the conversation: 

1) License scope: Redwood proposes a perpetual, non-transferable runtime license for the specific image and version deployed in your environment; territory limited to NexThera corporate entities named in the Order Form. We are open to a limited-transfer clause for M&A scenarios with prior notice and reasonable conditions.

2) Operator access: We prefer time-bound, audited remote support via bastion/jump sessions that are session-recorded and require mutual acceptance. For more sensitive customers we offer a complete operatorless runbook option (Redwood provides ops artifacts + training and no live access).

3) Evidence / escrow-lite: We can provide an attested snapshot deliverable (image hash + boot manifest + access logs) on a quarterly cadence or on-demand under escalation. We do not typically deposit source into escrow, but we can provide an encrypted runtime snapshot plus HSM attestation and a signed statement of the configuration and controls applied.

4) Audit windows & logs: We can export operational logs and session recordings to a customer S3 endpoint (or SFTP) for a configurable retention window. For on-prem installs the standard is 90 days rolling retention; longer retention is configurable as an add-on.

5) KMS/HSM custody: Supported: customer-managed KMS (recommended) or a split-custody HSM arrangement with attestation. We can support Bring-Your-Own-HSM (BYOH) patterns; in those cases Redwood holds no key material.

I’ve attached an initial draft addendum (Redwood_OnPrem_Addendum_Draft_20260210.docx) that captures the suggested language for sections 2.1 (License), 4.3 (Operator Access) and 6.1 (Evidence Delivery).

Can Rishi/Laura take the legal redlines and come back with contract language? Emma — would a technical workshop next week (Wed/Thu) be helpful to align on snapshot flow and delivery targets?

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_OnPrem_Addendum_Draft_20260210.docx
From: Emma Clark <emma.clark@nextherahealth.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Patrick Owens <patrick.owens@nextherahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deploy addendum — license boundary and evidence request

Aisha / Rishi / Laura — thanks, that helps. A few clarifications from our side after an internal compliance run: 

- Snapshot cadence: quarterly is acceptable as a baseline. For incident response we will need an on-demand certificate-backed snapshot delivered to a NexThera-controlled bucket within 48 hours.
- Transfer location: please confirm you can push to an S3 bucket in our account (we will supply temporary cross-account role) rather than Redwood delivering a copy directly to email.
- Licensing: Nexus governance requires a clause that restricts redeployment of the image to non-production systems only if explicitly authorized — can Redwood add that constraint?
- Indemnity/escrow: we will provide redlines that add an escrow-style deliverable for continuity (NOT source escrow) — expect a mark up from our procurement team shortly.

I’m attaching the procurement redlines we committed to circulate (NexThera_Redlines_20260211.docx). We’re aiming to get an internal approval to move to signature by 2/26, so timely responses on the snapshot SLA and key custody are critical.

Regards,
Emma Clark
Senior Counsel — Regulatory & Privacy
NexThera Health
attachments: NexThera_Redlines_20260211.docx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Clark <emma.clark@nextherahealth.com>, aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 16:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deploy addendum — license boundary and evidence request

Emma — appreciate the timeline. We reviewed your redlines and propose the following compromises in the addendum language (see attached draft for full text): 

- License: add express language that the runtime image provided to NexThera is licensed for internal production use for the named entities; any redeployment outside those named entities requires prior written consent. We can accept a carve-out allowing deployment to isolated non-production replicas for testing subject to controls (no cross-tenant export).

- Snapshot & delivery: Redwood agrees to provide an attested runtime snapshot on-demand within 48 hours, delivered to a customer-provided S3 endpoint with transfer integrity checks (signed manifest + hash). The quarterly scheduled snapshot will be included as part of the Dedicated deployment operational plan.

- Operator access: we will accept time-limited, role-scoped operator sessions limited to support tasks, with full session recording and audit trail. Where customers require zero operator access, Redwood will provide an operatorless delivery playbook and perform remote handoffs for escalations under predefined runbook steps.

- KMS/HSM custody: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS with clear responsibilities laid out in Section 6.2. For split custody we propose an HSM attestation requirement and an operational escrow key stewarding procedure; Redwood will not retain primary encryption keys in BYOH scenarios.

- Indemnity: we are open to narrowing indemnity to willful misconduct and gross negligence for software defects; broad IP indemnities as drafted will need more negotiation.

I attached a redline of the addendum with proposed contract text (Draft_Addendum_License_Scope_20260211.docx). If these points look acceptable in principle, we’ll incorporate into the MSA/Order Form and circulate a clean copy for signature.

Next steps: Aisha / Markus — can you confirm the technical delivery notes (snapshot manifest format, S3 transfer workflow, runbook references) so I can fold them into Section 4.3? Emma — if you can confirm acceptance of the indemnity scope by EOD Friday we can aim for the 2/26 signature target.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel — Contracts
Redwood Inference

Quick tech note from ops: we can produce a signed snapshot bundle with the following artifacts: image tar + boot manifest (SHA256) + runtime config + systemd/journal logs for the snapshot window + operator session recordings. Transfer mechanics: Redwood will push the bundle to a pre-authorized S3 bucket using multipart upload; we’ll include an S3 presigned manifest and a detached PGP signature for out-of-band verification.

We’ll also produce an automated runbook (runbook-snapshot-process.pdf) that covers: pre-snapshot checklist, snapshot creation steps, verification steps, and post-transfer validation. For HSM attestation we can provide an attestation quote from the HSM vendor and a signed statement of key handling steps.

Proposed times for a technical workshop to walk through the flow: Tues 2/17 10:00–11:00 ET or Wed 2/18 14:00–15:00 ET. Aisha — can you confirm which slot works and I’ll send a calendar invite + runbook link (drive above)?

—Markus
Lead, Production Services — Redwood Inference
